Entry requirements | University of Leeds
To study at Leeds, you’ll need to meet the academic entry requirements for your course and have a recognised English language qualification.
Course requirements
Use our
Course Search
to find the academic and English language entry requirements for your course.
Check the accepted qualifications for your country or region
.
If you have any questions about your qualifications,
email the International Office at internationaloffice@leeds.ac.uk
.
English language requirements
IELTS (International English Language Testing System)
We specify English language requirements in terms of IELTS. We accept both IELTS Academic and IELTS for UKVI (United Kingdom Visas and Immigration) (Academic). The test must be taken at a test centre.
We cannot accept results from an IELTS test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single IELTS test, or via a single test and One Skill Retake.
We also accept a range of other English language qualifications, which are listed in the next section.
Minimum requirements by study level
The following are the minimum English language requirements for each level of study. Some of our courses have higher English language requirements.
Check the entry requirements for your course via
Course Search
or, for postgraduate research programmes, the relevant faculty graduate school website.
We offer
pre-sessional English courses
to improve your academic English language level and help you prepare for study in the UK. You may be able to use a pre-sessional to meet the English language requirement for your course.

Undergraduate degrees
IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI (Academic):
6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in each component.
TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test):
80 overall with no less than 18 in reading, 17 in listening, 20 in speaking and 19 in writing (for tests taken before 21 January 2026) or 4 overall with no less than 4 in each component (for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026). We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single TOEFL iBT test taken in a test centre. We do not accept TOEFL MyBest scores or the TOEFL iBT Paper Edition.
PTE (Pearson Test of English) Academic
or
PTE Academic UKVI:
60 overall with no less than 59 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. We do not accept PTE Academic Online.
LanguageCert Academic or LanguageCert Academic SELT (Secure English Language Test):
65 overall with no less than 60 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. The test must have been taken in a test centre.
Oxford ELLT (English Language Level Test) Global:
6 overall with no less than 5 in each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study.
Oxford Test of English Advanced:
126 overall with no less than 111 in each component. We accept results from the full test of all four components or from individual tests of each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study.
A suitable Cambridge English qualification:
169 overall with no less than 162 in each component. The grade that you need for your course will determine which qualification you should take: B1 Preliminary, B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency. Check which qualification is relevant to your required grade on the Cambridge English website.
Trinity College London ISE (Integrated Skills in English):
Pass in ISE II or above. We cannot accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study.
NCUK English for Academic Purposes (EAP):
C overall with no less than D in each component. We cannot usually accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study.
NCUK English for Academic Purposes for Proficient Users (EAPPU):
C overall with no less than D in each component. We cannot usually accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study.
Study Group Academic English Skills (AES):
60% overall with no less than 50% in each component.

Pre-sessional English language courses
If you require a Student visa, you will need to have a Secure English Language Test (SELT) unless you are eligible for a combined Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). See our
guidance on visas for Language Centre students
. You do not need a SELT if you will study the pre-sessional online.
The minimum grade required in your English language qualification depends on the length of the pre-sessional and the degree you intend to study afterwards. Please check the
Language Centre website
for further information about entry requirements.
We accept the following SELTs:

4.0 overall with no less than 4.0 in each component.

English language requirements
IELTS (International English Language Testing System)
We specify English language requirements in terms of IELTS. We accept both IELTS Academic and IELTS for UKVI (United Kingdom Visas and Immigration) (Academic). The test must be taken at a test centre.
We cannot accept results from an IELTS test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single IELTS test, or via a single test and One Skill Retake.
We also accept a range of other English language qualifications, which are listed in the next section.
Minimum requirements by study level
The following are the minimum English language requirements for each level of study. Some of our courses have higher English language requirements.
Check the entry requirements for your course via
Course Search
or, for postgraduate research programmes, the relevant faculty graduate school website.
We offer
pre-sessional English courses
to improve your academic English language level and help you prepare for study in the UK. You may be able to use a pre-sessional to meet the English language requirement for your course.

You’ll have a network of wellbeing and support services dedicated to helping you get the most out of your time with us.
Help and advice
There are lots of resources and information available to support you.
Support and guidance
on the student website can provide help when you need it. You’ll find information about health concerns, disability support and more.
You can also get professional and confidential support and advice through
Leeds University Union’s student advice team
. The Union also provides peer-to-peer support through student-run helplines and online community groups. All their help is free and completely independent of the University.
Supporting your studies
You’ll be assigned an
academic personal tutor
who you’ll meet regularly throughout your studies. They will help you adjust to studying at university and guide your academic and personal development.
Mental health and wellbeing
You can access free professional and confidential
counselling, wellbeing and mental health support
through groups, workshops, single-session consultations, short-term counselling and online self-help resources.
If you need longer-term support or treatment, we’ll help you find the most appropriate NHS (National Health Service) or voluntary sector services.
Support for disabled students
If you’re a disabled student, we’ll work with your academic school and other University services to ensure that we meet your needs and make reasonable adjustments to support you with your studies.
Additional funding
might be available to pay for specialist academic-related support and equipment.
If you are an international student, you should talk to your sponsor about extra funding for these items or, if you don’t have a sponsor,
contact Disability Services
.
Don’t wait until you start your course to contact us. It can take several months to arrange support, so it is important that you contact us as early as possible.
Please
email Disability Services via disability@leeds.ac.uk
so we can discuss your needs and additional arrangements.
Support for care-experienced or estranged students
You could get extra support if you’re currently in care, have experience of being in care or you’re estranged from your parents (meaning you have no relationship or physical or financial support from them). Find out more about support for
care-experienced and estranged students
.
Multi-faith campus
There are
spaces on campus for prayer and quiet contemplation
. If you practise a faith, you can be confident you’ll be able to follow your beliefs in Leeds.
Leeds University Union’s clubs include
faith-related student societies
you can join.
International student support
We’ve been welcoming international students for over 100 years, so you can be sure of experienced help and support.

immigration experts

We have overseas offices in China, Nigeria, South Asia and Southeast Asia, as well as a global network of representatives who can advise you about studying here. Find out how to
contact a representative in your country or region
.
Our
prepare for Leeds

You

Living costs and budgeting | University of Leeds
To make sure you have enough money for your accommodation, living and study costs at university, it’s a good idea to plan your budget early.
The information on this page is provided as a guideline only
, based on average spending. You should
calculate your own budget
.
If you are an international student, and you have met
financial requirements for your visa
, you should still work out a personal budget separately.
Budget for the amount you would need without getting a job. You may be able to work during your studies, but it will depend on the demands of your course and, if you are an international student,
whether your visa allows you to work in the UK
.
Be aware that living costs may change and be affected by changes in currency exchange rates.
Estimated costs per week
The following tables are estimates for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available. The actual amount will depend on your accommodation type and availability, and your lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
All University accommodation costs include household bills and (except family accommodation) gym membership. Some private accommodation costs include household bills.
Accommodation
Estimated cost per week
University accommodation, self-catered
£117 to £265
University accommodation, catered
£205 to £273
Private accommodation, self-catered
£110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications)

Estimated cost per week
Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products
£31 to £38

£14 to £17
Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone
£44 to £68

Tuition fees.
University accommodation
or
private accommodation
. If you plan to bring your family, read
information on family accommodation and the costs
.

Household bills, including energy (gas and/or electricity), water and internet, if not included in your accommodation. These are included in most University accommodation and sometimes included in private accommodation, but not always, so you should check.
Groceries such as food and cleaning supplies.
Buying a laptop (unless you are bringing a reliable laptop suitable for university use with you).
Guidance about bringing your laptop to university
.
Immigration-related costs
and
your flight to the UK and travel to Leeds
, if you’re an international student.
Travel to visit home or family during breaks (which may include international travel) and
local transport around Leeds
.
Childcare costs
, if you plan to bring your family.
General study costs, such as printing, photocopying and stationery. You can borrow books from our libraries and use University PCs for free.
Costs associated with your course. Some will be optional and depend on your modules, but may include: studying abroad, placements and field trips, conferences and skills days, professional body membership fees, specialist clothing, equipment and project materials. You can check
Course Search
for details.
Mobile phone
.
Activities on campus and in the city. There are also free activities organised by the University and
Leeds University Union
.
A TV licence
, if you watch or record live programmes on TV and streaming services or use BBC iPlayer. You won’t need one for on-demand only streaming services such as Netflix but you will need a subscription.

English language requirements | University of Leeds
If you are applying to spend a semester or a year studying abroad at the University of Leeds, you must make sure you meet our English language entry requirements.
English language entry requirements vary according to which teaching school you will be taking modules in. This will determine whether you need to prove that you meet:
the
standard English language requirements
or
the
higher English language requirements
.
In some circumstances, we also accept
alternative English language evidence
.
If you do not meet our English language requirements, we offer
pre-sessional English language courses
.
Check your language requirements
Complete this survey to receive an email outlining what English Language evidence you need to provide with your application based on your personal circumstances.
Standard English language requirements
The majority of teaching schools at the University of Leeds expect study abroad students to meet the standard English language requirements. These are:
IELTS (International English Language Testing System)
Overall: 6.0
Listening, reading, speaking and writing: 5.5
TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test)
0-120 Scale
(Tests taken before 21 January 2026)
Overall: 80
Listening: 17
Reading: 18
Writing: 19
Speaking: 20
1-6 Scale
(Tests taken on or after 21 January 2026)
Overall: 4
Listening, reading, speaking and writing: 4
You will need to provide evidence that you meet these requirements when you submit your application to the University of Leeds.
Higher English language requirements
The following teaching schools have higher English language entry requirements:
School of Fine Art, History of Art and Cultural Studies (module code ARTF)
School of Media and Communication (module code COMM)
School of English (module code ENGL)
School of Law (module code LAW)
Department of Linguistics and Phonetics (module code LING)
Leeds University Business School (module code LUBS)
School of Philosophy, Religion and History of Science (module code PHIL)
School of Politics and International Studies (module code PIED)
Language Centre (module code ELU)
Level 2 and above only
If you want to take modules in these schools, you must have attained the higher entry requirement in one of the following qualifications by the time you apply to Leeds. The higher entry requirements are:
IELTS
Overall: 6.5
Listening, reading, speaking and writing: 6.0
TOEFL (iBT)
0-120 Scale
(Tests taken before 21 January 2026)
Overall: 88
Listening: 19
Reading: 20
Writing: 21
Speaking: 22
1-6 Scale
(Tests taken on or after 21 January 2026)
Overall: 4.5
Listening, reading and speaking: 4
Writing: 4.5
Please note that from 2024, if you need UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) sponsorship for a student visa, we will no longer consider online tests of English, such as TOEFL iBT Home Edition.
Alternative English language evidence
If you do not have a valid IELTS or TOEFL certificate, there are alternative types of English language evidence that we can accept, including English studied as part of some high school qualifications.
We recommend that you:
Check the
accepted qualifications for your country or region
. We may accept your high school English qualification if listed here and you attained the minimum score given under ‘English Language minimum for undergraduate study’.
Check the
English language requirements for undergraduate degrees
to see if we accept your English language certificate. If you intend to take modules in the schools that have the higher English language requirement, your certificate will need to prove that you meet the English language requirements listed under ‘Masters degrees’.
If your degree is taught and examined entirely in English and you will have completed two years of study on the programme by the time you arrive in Leeds, you can provide a letter from your home university confirming this.
If you do not meet our direct entry language requirements
If you do not meet our standard or higher language requirements for direct entry, you can take a
pre-sessional English language course
directly before the start of semester 1 and semester 2 with our Language Centre.
The duration of the pre-sessional English language course you need to complete will be based on your existing English language scores as well as the academic schools you wish to take modules in. After you complete your pre-sessional course, you will need to meet the English language requirements for study abroad programmes.
How to apply for a pre-sessional English language course
You do not need to apply separately for the pre-sessional course – apply for a combined pre-sessional and study abroad programme via the
Study Abroad/Exchange application form
.
If you are applying for a pre-sessional English Language course before your semester or year of study abroad, you must apply with a SELT (Secure English Language Test) such as IELTS for UKVI.
Pre-sessional course fees
Pre-sessional courses are not usually included in exchange programme tuition fee waiver arrangements. Find out more about
pre-sessional English language programmes
.

If you’re an international student and you don’t currently meet the
entry requirements

If you are UK student, our

Undergraduate international foundation routes
University of Leeds International Foundation Year
The Bachelor degree with integrated
International Foundation Year
begins with the International Foundation Year programme. It helps to prepare you for the first year of undergraduate study.
Based on our campus, all your teaching will be delivered by University of Leeds academics and you’ll be a full University student with access to all our facilities and accommodation.
Once you have successfully completed the initial foundation year, you’ll progress onto one of more than 150 undergraduate degrees.
Study Group: Leeds International Study Centre
The
Leeds International Study Centre International Foundation Year
delivered by Study Group allows you to progress to year one of a range of undergraduate degrees at the University of Leeds.
It will help you to develop the skills and knowledge you need to succeed at university, providing flexible entry requirements and start dates in September or January.
The Leeds International Study Centre also offers
International Year One programmes
in certain subjects, allowing progression to year two of some undergraduate degrees at the University of Leeds.
For both of these programme options, you’ll be taught by Study Group staff and will be based at the Centre’s teaching facilities in Leeds.
Northern Consortium UK (NCUK)
The University of Leeds is an owner member of
NCUK
, which delivers
undergraduate International Foundation Years
and
International Year One programmes
at teaching centres worldwide.
Successful completion of NCUK qualifications enables progression onto a range of undergraduate courses at the University of Leeds.
Postgraduate international foundation routes
Northern Consortium UK (NCUK)
NCUK
delivers
Masters Preparation programmes
at teaching centres worldwide.
Successful completion of an NCUK Masters Preparation programme allows you to progress onto a range of postgraduate courses at the University of Leeds.
Study Group: Leeds International Study Centre
The
Leeds International Study Centre Pre-Masters Programme
, delivered by Study Group, allows you to progress to Postgraduate degrees in Business at the University of Leeds. It will help you to develop the skills and knowledge you need to succeed at university, providing flexible entry requirements, and start dates in September or January.
For this Pre-Masters Programme, you’ll be taught by Study Group staff and will be based at the Centre’s teaching facilities in the city of Leeds.

Students’ Union | University of Leeds
You’ll join one of the best and most active students’ unions in the country. Its mission is to make sure you love your time at Leeds.
Leeds University Union
(LUU) brings together our student community and is 100% student-led. With more than 1,000 student reps, you can be sure your voice will be heard on the things that matter to you.
The Union building is in the middle of campus. It’s a place where you can meet, work, socialise and relax.
There are shops, cafes, bars, clubs and flexible spaces where you can organise your own event. Top bands and artists play there too.
LUU is independent of the University of Leeds and offers free and impartial help and advice if things don't go quite to plan.
You can also
find part-time work through Joblink
.
Take a 360° tour: Leeds University Union
Clubs and societies
“I spend most of my free time in the societies. It’s a great way to relax and there’s a real sense of community. I’ve made lots of friends through the K-pop dance society and this has exposed me to different cultures.”
Leeds University Union runs more than 300 student-led
clubs and societies
, so you’ll find something whatever your interests.
Football, debating, theatre, gaming, dance, photography and even skydiving are just a few of your options. There are also different national and faith societies too.
If you and your friends want to take part in an activity which doesn’t have a club, the Union will help you set one up.
They’re a great way to meet new people and create some amazing memories. You’ll also develop valuable skills while you’re studying, like teamworking and leadership.
Most academic schools also have their own societies, so you can get to know people from other courses and year groups.

International preparation and arrival | University of Leeds
Starting university in a new country is a big step. We’re here to help you feel confident and prepared for your move to Leeds.
From preparing for your move to settling into life on campus, you’ll have access to guidance, practical support and opportunities to help you feel confident, welcome and ready to begin your journey.
Preparing for Leeds
Visa and immigration
Find out which type of visa you’ll need
to study at the University of Leeds, based on your programme, length of your course or research period.
You will be able to
apply for your visa
when you receive your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). The earliest we can issue your CAS is six months before the start of your course.
Our guidance video takes you through the student visa application process, including obtaining your CAS, preparing your finances, completing your application, and submitting it successfully. Watch the recording on
YouTube
or
Bilibili
.
Our
Student Visa Advice service
provides free guidance from experienced immigration advisers, offering the support you need to complete your application with confidence.
Connect with students
Our
Link to Leeds Ambassadors
are current students who have already experienced the journey to studying in the UK.
Join Link to Leeds events
and learn more about what it’s like to live and study in Leeds, directly from current students. Connect with them to get practical advice and support as you prepare for your life in Leeds.
Follow Link to Leeds on Instagram
.
Pre-arrival webinars
We offer a range of pre-arrival webinars to help you prepare for life in Leeds.
Attend pre arrival webinars as part of
International orientation
to help you prepare for life in Leeds. These sessions cover practical topics such as banking, healthcare, jobs and careers, as well as preparing for academic life, helping you transition smoothly to studying and living in the UK.
International offer holder events
We host a range of
events and activities for international offer holders
, to help answer any questions you have before you start your studies with us.
Our activities include global webinars, Q&As, Offer Holder groups and events in your region or country.
Jumpstart: our pre-arrival careers portal
Jumpstart is our careers support platform for international students. It is designed to help you feel confident and prepared before you arrive in Leeds.
It provides expert guidance, tools to help you prepare for your career, and current UK and global job opportunities.
​It includes:
a template to help you build a UK-style CV
part‑time job listings
tips on getting started with LinkedIn
career preparation resources
a guide to visas and working.
If you’re an international offer holder, you’ll have already received an email from us about how to access Jumpstart.
If you have any questions or would like more information on Jumpstart,
email the Careers Centre at careerscentre@leeds.ac.uk
.
Arriving on campus
When to arrive
Arriving in Leeds in good time will help you settle in and start your studies smoothly.
Find out more about
when to arrive
this academic year.
Travelling to Leeds
To help you have a smooth arrival in Leeds, all new international students can book our
free airport pick-up service
from Leeds Bradford or Manchester Airport.
For anyone travelling from any other UK airport, we have more
information about travelling to Leeds
to help you arrange your journey to our campus.
Settling in
The Student Information Service
The Student Information Service
provides year-round support to applicants, students, researchers and alumni, offering guidance and answering questions from pre-arrival through to graduation.
Before you arrive, you can contact the team by phone with any queries. Once on campus, you can contact the team by email or phone, or visit one of the Student Information Points in person.
International orientation
If you’re starting in September
International Orientation
takes place in September one week before Welcome Week, our main intake period.
Arriving early gives you the chance to explore campus while it’s quieter, take part in tailored sessions, complete essential tasks and connect with both new and current students at a relaxed pace.
It also means you can enjoy two full weeks of social events and activities, ensuring you feel settled, confident and fully prepared before your course begins.
What to expect from International Orientation:
online and in‑person sessions providing practical information, insights from current students, and support to help you navigate cultural change with confidence
campus, city chase and faith tours, offering a fun way to discover our campus and city of Leeds
social events to help you connect with our student community and start making friends from day one
school inductions to welcome you in your School and introduce you to your academic community.
If you’re starting in January
If you're an exchange student or postgraduate researcher starting in January, International Orientation will run again for the January intake.
During this time, there will also be additional campus tours and events as part of the Fresh Start Festival, giving you plenty of opportunities to meet other students, explore campus, and become familiar with your new surroundings.
If you’re starting at any other time
If you’re a postgraduate researcher or international student starting at any other point in the year, you will be able to:
access recordings and presentations slides from International Orientation and explore resources in your own time
access self-guided campus tours
take part in campus and city events and activities hosted by Leeds University Union.
Opportunities to connect
There are many opportunities to connect when you arrive in Leeds and throughout your time at university. Whether you’re looking to meet new people, find your community or try something new, you’ll find plenty of ways to get involved, including:
Clubs and societies
– Leeds University Union (LUU) runs more than 350 groups for sport, music, gaming, volunteering and more.
Buddy Scheme
– get matched with another student who shares your interests and study level. Buddies meet up, swap tips and join free socials together.
Global Café
– every Monday excluding bank holidays. Drop in for free drinks, relaxed chat and new friends in our diverse community.
Events offered through
Leeds University Union (LUU) Engage
, International Orientation, Welcome Week and throughout the year.
Experiences and opportunities
– connect with new people, find your community, and share experiences that can lead to lasting friendships and personal growth.
Support and guidance
Explore the dedicated
academic and wellbeing support
available to help you make the most of your time here and ensure a positive experience throughout your stay.
Disability support in the UK may differ from what you’re used to. In the UK, the term disability includes a wide range of both visible and invisible conditions.
Learn more about how disability is understood in the UK and the additional support available
.
Skill@library
provides one-to-one sessions, workshops and online resources to support your academic development.
The Language Zone
provides free support, activities and resources to help you improve your English language skills independently.
Getting help with preparation and arrival
We will be in touch with you from the start and throughout your stay in Leeds. In the months leading up to your arrival we will remind you about the key tasks you need to complete to prepare for your studies. In the meantime, you can:
Explore our
Welcome guidance
. This explains the processes you need to follow to ensure you are fully enrolled and ready to begin your academic journey. It also reminds you of opportunities and events to join in the first few weeks.
Contact our Student Information Service (SIS)
with questions at any point of your journey. Our Student Information Service is here to help with any questions you may have and can connect you with the right team at the University of Leeds for support before you arrive and throughout your student journey.

Visas for Language Centre students | University of Leeds
The visa you need depends on the English language course you will study, the length of the course, and the English Language qualification that you have.
There are three types of immigration status to choose from: the
Student visa
, the
Short-term study visa
and
Standard Visitor
.
Find out which visa you will need based on the type of pre-sessional and length of the English language course you will be studying:
Academic Year Pre-sessionals
If you are studying for more than 11 months
If you are studying for a period of more than 11 months, you must apply for a Student visa before travelling to the UK. Read our step-by-step guide on
how to apply for a Student visa
We recommend that you apply for a Student visa if:
You have an offer to start an academic degree programme immediately after the completion of your English language course.
Your course is longer than six months and family members are accompanying you as
dependants
.
You wish to work part time.
To be eligible for a Student visa you will need to have a Secure English Language Test (SELT). You can find information about the English Language qualifications that we accept, including SELTs, on our
entry requirements page
.
You must remain on your pre-sessional English programme if you hold a Student visa, even if you obtain a higher IELTS score during the course. This is because if you stop studying, the University must report this to UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI and your visa will be cancelled. You must also return home as you cannot extend your visa inside the UK due to not completing the course for which your visa was issued.
Please note that Student visas can be extended from inside the UK if they meet the UKVI’s Academic Progression and other requirements.
If you are studying for six to 11 months
If you are studying an English language course for a period of six to 11 months, you can apply for a
Short-term study visa
or
Student visa
Work is not permitted on the Short-term study visa and you cannot stay longer than 11 months or switch into another immigration route on this visa in the UK.
Short-term study visas require you to leave the UK and return home after completion of your English language course to apply for a Student visa for your academic degree programme.
Find further information about short-term study visas on the
UK Council for International Student Affairs (UKCISA) website
.
For further information on Student visas please read the guidance on applying for ‘If you are studying for more than 11 months’ in the previous section on this page.
If you are studying for less than six months
If you are studying an English language course for less than six months, you can apply to come to the UK as a
Standard Visitor
or with a
Student visa
.
Depending on your nationality, you may be required to either apply for a visa or an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before you can travel to the UK as a Standard Visitor.
Standard Visitor is suitable for most Language Centre students, but a Student visa allows you to work part-time while you are studying.
If you come to the UK as a Standard Visitor, you will be required to leave the UK and return home after completion of the English language course to apply for a Student visa for your academic degree programme.
Read our comparison guide to help you
decide which visa to apply for
.
Summer Pre-Sessionals
Please note, we recommend that you apply for a
Student visa
if you are studying a summer pre-sessional, as you will also have an offer to start an academic degree programme immediately after the completion of your English language course. This visa can be extended in the UK, avoiding delays in arriving for and starting your chosen degree programme.
To be eligible for a Student visa, you will need to have a Secure English Language Test (SELT), unless you are eligible to receive a combined CAS. You can find information about the English Language qualifications that we accept, including SELTs, on our
entry requirements page
.
If you are studying an Academic English for Undergraduate Studies Pre-sessional
You will need to provide us a Secure English Language Test on CEFR B2 level, taken in the last 2 years of the course start date and apply for a
Student visa
for the pre-sessional course only. Your Student visa can be extended from inside the UK, if you meet the UKVI’s Academic Progression and other requirements.
If you are studying a Research Pre-sessional
As this English language course is less than six months, you can apply to come to the UK as a
Standard Visitor
or with a
Student visa
.
Standard Visitor is suitable for most Language Centre students, but a Student visa allows you to work part-time while you are studying.
If you come to the UK as a Standard Visitor, you will be required to leave the UK and return home after completion of the English language course to apply for a Student visa for your academic degree programme.
You will only be eligible for a combined CAS for your Pre-sessional and degree programme if your research degree offer is unconditional.
If you are studying the Online Pre-sessional
No visa is required to study this course. You must successfully complete the online pre-sessional and receive your CAS for your degree programme before you can travel to the UK. It is your responsibility to arrange your travel and visa appointment, and the Language Centre cannot be held liable if you arrive too late to start your degree course. If you arrive late, please contact the admissions team using the contact details in your degree offer letter. You also check
UKVI’s visa processing times
before you apply.
If you are studying one of the Content-based Academic English for Postgraduate Studies pre-sessionals
10 week pre-sessional
If your offer is unconditional or conditional only on English, you will be eligible for a combined CAS for your pre-sessional and Masters course and will need to apply for a
Student visa
.
If you have a conditional Masters offer with an academic condition, you will need to provide us a Secure English Language Test on CEFR B2 level, taken in the last 2 years of the course start date and apply for a
Student visa
for the pre-sessional course only. Your Student visa can be extended from inside the UK, if you meet the UKVI’s Academic Progression and other requirements. You may be eligible to receive a combined CAS if you meet our deadlines. Find further information on the
deadlines for pre-sessional courses
page.
6 week pre-sessional
You will only be eligible for a combined CAS for your pre-sessional and masters course if you meet your academic conditions by the deadline. If you are unable to do this, you will need to provide a SELT and request a pre-sessional-only CAS via the
application portal
to apply for a
Student visa
, which can be extended from inside the UK, if you meet the UKVI’s Academic Progression and other requirements. Find further information on the
deadlines for pre-sessional courses
page.
Who do I contact if I need visa advice?
If you have a visa question, or would like your visa application checked before you submit it, please contact the
Student Visa Advice service
.

Entry requirements for those with UK and International Baccalaureate qualifications
IGCSE
We will consider students who have completed a minimum of five IGCSEs with a grade 7 or A, including in relevant subjects. The specific subjects will depend on the intended undergraduate degree programme.
AS Levels
We will consider students who have completed AS Levels and achieved a grade B in at least two subjects. The specific subjects will depend on the intended undergraduate degree programme.
International Baccalaureate
We will consider students who have completed the International Baccalaureate and reached a minimum Grade of 26 points overall with grade 4 at Standard Level or 3 at Higher Level in two subjects. The specific subjects will depend on the intended undergraduate degree programme.
English language requirements
Arts and Social Science, Business, Design, Engineering and Science routes
IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI (Academic)
: 5.5 overall with no less than 5.5 in each component. We cannot accept results from an IELTS test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single IELTS test, or via a single test and One Skill Retake. The test must be taken at a test centre.
TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test)
: TOEFL iBT at 72 overall with 17 in listening, 18 in reading, 20 in speaking and 19 in writing (for tests taken before 21 January 2026) = 4 overall with 4 in each component (for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026). We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single TOEFL iBT test taken in a test centre. We do not accept TOEFL MyBest scores or the TOEFL iBT Paper Edition.

International campus tours | University of Leeds
If you’re visiting the UK, our bespoke campus tours are a great way to get a feel for life at Leeds.
Each tour is led by one of our friendly student ambassadors and takes place mainly outside.
Our campus tours are not course specific, so you won’t be able to visit any academic schools but we’ll do our best to tailor the tour to your needs.
When you’re booking a campus tour, you’ll need to give at least a week's notice, so we can make sure everything is ready for when you arrive. Campus tours are not available at weekends.

About Leeds International Summer School
Leeds International Summer School (LISS) combines world-class tuition and academic field trips with exciting excursions and social events.
Choose from a diverse range of academic modules, meet interesting people from around the world and immerse yourself in British culture and society.
LISS is open to students or recent graduates from universities across the globe. Join us for the full four-week programme or a two-week block.
Our next summer school will run from 3 July–31 July 2027 (block one: 3 July–17 July, block two: 18 July–31 July).

Sport and fitness | University of Leeds
Whether you want to keep fit, play sport socially or compete at a high level, you’ll find everything you need at Leeds to keep active and feel your best.
The Edge
You’ll get discounted access to our indoor sports facility on campus,
The Edge
. If you’re living in university accommodation you’ll get an
Edge Premium membership
included within your stay.
It has a 250-station gym, a 25m swimming pool, sauna and steam rooms and a climbing wall. There are also squash courts and sports halls where you can play badminton, netball, five-a-side football and more.
There are also studios offering a variety of exercise classes during term time. You could also access the dedicated personal training and strength and conditioning rooms with qualified trainers available when you need some extra motivation.

You could make use of our excellent outdoor sports facilities at nearby

and

Our
outdoor centre in the Yorkshire Dales
is perfect for activities like hiking, caving, mountain biking and climbing. There’s also a
boat house
next to Thwaite Mills in Stourton with direct access to the canal for rowing.

At Leeds you’ll be able to get involved in
sports clubs and societies
whatever your ability or ambition. You could get involved in a range of activities from surfing to dance to martial arts.

coaching, officiating and leadership programmes
, or get in involved a local or international community sports project.

will support you to achieve academic and sporting excellence.

Foundation courses
Foundation year courses for UK students
A foundation year is the first year of an extended degree. It’s an extra year of study at the start of an undergraduate course which will help you to develop the study skills you need to succeed on your chosen degree.
There are many reasons you may decide to study a foundation year such as not having the qualifications needed or not being predicted the required grades for your chosen degree, wanting additional time to prepare for your degree or wanting to do something new.
From day one, our foundation year students are part of the Leeds student community and you’ll be able to make the most of all the opportunities we offer.

Representatives in your country or region | University of Leeds
We work with representatives worldwide who can provide you with comprehensive support in applying to the University of Leeds. Use the contact details on this page to find an appointed agent in your city, country or region.
Our representatives (also called agents) are based around the world and act as officially appointed representatives of the University of Leeds. They have been provided with expert guidance on our courses, admissions processes, and policies. They can advise you throughout the application process. Some agents will offer face-to-face support and have offices in the town or city where you live, while others may use digital channels to communicate with you.
The University pays commission to agents if you receive their support and enrol on a course at the University, but using their services won't affect your chances of being accepted. We work with agents because it extends our global presence, and many students find it beneficial to receive support when applying to university.
Please note:
If an agent is not listed on this page, the University does
not
maintain a relationship with them or endorse their services.
How our agents can help you
Agents can help you:
decide which country and which University is the best study destination for you
find a course that best fits your needs
understand the suitability of your qualifications and background (please note that our admissions team makes the final decision on your offer)
navigate through the application process including preparing and submitting necessary documents and details. However, you (the applicant) remain ultimately responsible for your account and the management of communications
by liaising with the University on your behalf, provided you’ve permitted the agent to be listed as your approved representative
with your visa application, including advising on the documents you need to provide
understand travel advice and guidance before your departure.
Agent responsibilities
We expect our representatives to be reliable, honest, and trustworthy providers of advice and guidance to you and in all aspects of their business, including:
always being honest and transparent when communicating information about the University to you; not knowingly providing false, incomplete or misleading information
acting in the best interests of you at all times, providing accurate information that allows you to make informed decisions
always respecting your choices
not making offers of admission on behalf of the University
not entering into any contract or agreement on behalf of the University
not defaming or inaccurately conveying the reputation or interests of any higher education institutions.
Advice for choosing an agent
At the University of Leeds, we commit to the
UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF)
and pledge to create and maintain best practice in agent management to encourage informed decision-making and transparency.
If you are considering using the services of an agent, we encourage you to read the
British Council’s student guide to choosing an education agent
.
Some agents charge students a counselling fee, so we advise you to confirm all costs in advance. You should also check if an agent is authorised to represent the University of Leeds. In some instances, our agents may work with other agents (sometimes referred to as sub-agents), but we will not have contracts with these partners, and are unable to support them in the same way.
Never pay any course deposits or tuition fee payments to an agent – you should always pay these directly to the University.
You can only work with one representative to support you with your application to Leeds. If you are experiencing issues with your nominated agent and you are unable to resolve the issues with them directly, or you want to change your nominated agent, please
email the International Office at internationaloffice@leeds.ac.uk

International students | University of Leeds
International students
International study at Leeds
Our global reputation for teaching and research attracts students from around the world. Leeds is a truly multicultural campus with more than 14,400 international students from 137 countries, in a student-friendly city.
Top 100 university in the world
We are a Russell Group and a leading UK research university, so research is at the heart of our teaching, whatever your level of study. You’ll study among inspirational academics, world experts who share your passion for your subject.

Your future career
We’ll help you reach your potential by challenging you, academically and personally, and helping you develop your employability skills.
Read more about your future career opportunities
You’ll have lots of opportunities to build your practical and transferable skills, and to benefit from careers events and advice. Project work, fieldwork or work placements are included in many of our undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Funding for students with dependents | University of Leeds
If you have children or adults who depend on you, you may be able to access government funding to provide extra financial support while you study.
Students with dependent children
You can get individual advice from the
Student Advice Centre
in Leeds University Union about whether financial support is available.
Our Lifelong Learning Centre has information about the practical help we offer, including childcare, accommodation for families, and campus facilities for students with young children.
If you are studying an undergraduate full-time course, you could be eligible for the
Childcare Grant
and
Parents’ Learning Allowance
.
Students with adult dependants
If you are studying an undergraduate full-time course, you may be able to apply for the
Adult Dependants' Grant
. You cannot apply for the Adult Dependents’ Grant if you are taking out a postgraduate loan.

Fees and funding | University of Leeds
There are many ways you can fund your Masters studies.
The two main costs to consider are tuition fees and living costs. It’s a good idea to plan your finances before starting your course.
Masters funding
Check your eligibility for scholarships and bursaries at Leeds, and explore a range of external funding sources.
Top tips for funding your Masters
Read our guide to creating a personalised funding package.
Paying your tuition fees
Details of your tuition fees are included with your offer letter. If you have any specific questions, please contact the admissions team in your school or department using the contact details on your offer letter.
For questions about payment, please
phone the Student Finance (Fees) team on +44 (0)113 343 6700
or
email the Student Finance (Fees) team at pgfees@leeds.ac.uk
.
If you require a Student visa to study in the UK, once you have accepted an unconditional offer you will be asked to pay a tuition fee deposit or provide evidence that you are fully funded by a University-recognised sponsor or scholarship. For details about this, visit
Tuition fee deposits for Masters applicants
.
Self-funding students
For information on how to pay as a self-funding student, visit our
paying fees and charges page
.
Sponsored students
For information on what you and your sponsor must provide, visit our
sponsored students page
.
Cost of living
Budgeting is important throughout your studies, and we have guidance and support to help you make the most of your money.
Our
Living costs and budgeting
page includes a budget calculator to find out how much money you’re likely to spend in a typical week at Leeds.
You can also read our
student blogs
for a real-life guide to living costs while at university.
Get information on how to budget, save money and where to access financial support on our
Money management
page.
Leeds University Union
also offers independent advice and help with any issues you may face as a student, including money matters.

Industry experience opportunities | University of Leeds
Postgraduate study at Leeds develops your academic knowledge and gives you the experience and connections you need to accelerate your career.
We offer guaranteed industry experience for the majority of our on-campus taught postgraduate courses.
Global Industry Programme
Our Global Industry Programme will give you the opportunity to apply your learning to solve real-world challenges. You can gain consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation as part of your postgraduate study.
You’ll engage with a business, developing skills to enhance your employability, building connections and gaining the hands-on experience companies are looking for.
Our fully online, flexible programme is designed to fit around your studies and is open to all subject areas, offering practical industry experience before you graduate.
You’ll build international, cross-cultural networks, with opportunities in areas including digital marketing, business growth, sustainability and artificial intelligence.
How the Global Industry Programme works
Working in a student team, you'll help a company solve a real business problem.
You’ll receive a live company brief, then research, analyse and develop solutions before presenting your findings in a professional consultancy report.
You’ll receive feedback on your work to enhance your skills and confidence, and graduate from the programme with a digital badge and certificate to boost your CV and showcase your experience.
The programme will help you develop problem-solving, teamwork and other professional skills that will benefit you in any career, and prepare you to make a bigger impact in the world.
You’re guaranteed a place on the programme if you’re a taught postgraduate student, whether you're from the UK or overseas. However, this doesn’t apply if you’re studying the Leeds MBA or you're part of the Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences (EPS), as EPS students have access to a
dedicated virtual work experience programme
embedded within the course.
It was a really good experience, meeting some great people and interacting with a really interesting sustainability-related startup company. It also helped me build conﬁdence with my ability to develop reports and professional communication skills with clients and my teammates.
Career support and opportunities
You will have access to a range of career support throughout your studies, including:
dedicated careers guidance
AI-driven tools to help shape your CV, cover letters and LinkedIn profiles
careers fairs and employer events for opportunities in the UK and overseas
support with mock interviews, assessment centres and psychometric tests.
Take part in opportunities to build confidence, connections and careers, including:
leadership programmes
mentoring
paid work and internships on and off campus
research conferences and events
volunteering.
More information about the Careers Service
Learn more about career enhancement opportunities in the
Careers section of the Students website
.

Wellbeing and support | University of Leeds
You’ll have a network of wellbeing and support services dedicated to helping you get the most out of your time with us.
Help and advice
There are lots of resources and information available to support you.
Support and guidance
on the student website can provide help when you need it. You’ll find information about health concerns, disability support and more.
You can also get professional and confidential support and advice through
Leeds University Union’s student advice team
. The Union also provides peer-to-peer support through student-run helplines and online community groups. All their help is free and completely independent of the University.
Supporting your studies
You’ll be assigned an
academic personal tutor
who you’ll meet regularly throughout your studies. They will help you adjust to studying at university and guide your academic and personal development.
Mental health and wellbeing
You can access free professional and confidential
counselling, wellbeing and mental health support
through groups, workshops, single-session consultations, short-term counselling and online self-help resources.
If you need longer-term support or treatment, we’ll help you find the most appropriate NHS (National Health Service) or voluntary sector services.
Support for disabled students
If you’re a disabled student, we’ll work with your academic school and other University services to ensure that we meet your needs and make reasonable adjustments to support you with your studies.
Additional funding
might be available to pay for specialist academic-related support and equipment.
If you are an international student, you should talk to your sponsor about extra funding for these items or, if you don’t have a sponsor,
contact Disability Services
.
Don’t wait until you start your course to contact us. It can take several months to arrange support, so it is important that you contact us as early as possible.
Please
email Disability Services via disability@leeds.ac.uk
so we can discuss your needs and additional arrangements.
Support for care-experienced or estranged students
You could get extra support if you’re currently in care, have experience of being in care or you’re estranged from your parents (meaning you have no relationship or physical or financial support from them). Find out more about support for
care-experienced and estranged students
.
Multi-faith campus
There are
spaces on campus for prayer and quiet contemplation
. If you practise a faith, you can be confident you’ll be able to follow your beliefs in Leeds.
Leeds University Union’s clubs include
faith-related student societies
you can join.
International student support
We’ve been welcoming international students for over 100 years, so you can be sure of experienced help and support.
Before you arrive
Our team of
immigration experts
can give you free advice on immigration law and requirements. They can also help you with the visa application process.
We have overseas offices in China, Nigeria, South Asia and Southeast Asia, as well as a global network of representatives who can advise you about studying here. Find out how to
contact a representative in your country or region
.
Our
prepare for Leeds
pages will help you arrange your journey to Leeds.
Arriving in Leeds
We offer an
airport pick-up service
from Leeds Bradford and Manchester Airports on key dates.
You
’
ll also be invited to
international orientation
, a free programme of talks, tours, events and social activities to help you settle into life in Leeds. This is the ideal way to learn more about the opportunities available at Leeds, meet people and start making connections.

Paying for online courses | University of Leeds
This page outlines how to pay for online postgraduate courses with the University of Leeds, including module by module payments, postgraduate loan payment plans, and payments by sponsors.
Fees for each course are available on
Course Search
.
You will need to confirm how you will be paying your fees before you register for the course.
Paying module by module
Some of our online courses allow you to pay your fees module by module.
Online courses that offer module by module payments
Artificial Intelligence MSc
Artificial Intelligence Postgraduate Certificate
Data Science (Statistics) MSc
Disability Studies, Rights and Inclusion Postgraduate Certificate
Disability Studies, Rights and Inclusion Postgraduate Diploma
Disability Studies, Rights and Inclusion MSc
Engineering Management MSc
Engineering Management Postgraduate Certificate
Genomic Medicine with Data Science MSc
Genomic Medicine with Data Science Postgraduate Certificate
Global Health MSc
Global Health Postgraduate Certificate
​​​​​
If your course fees can be paid module by module, the fee payments break down as follows:
the first payment is required before you begin the course;
then pay for each module as you take it. There are typically nine or ten modules depending on the course structure;
the final payment is for the project module fee, if applicable.
You can
pay for a module through our online store
by credit card or PayPal. You will need your student number.
Please note, if you are receiving a postgraduate student loan, or are being sponsored as a student (for example by your employer) and require an invoice you will not be able to pay your fees module by module.
Paying with a postgraduate loan (UK only)
If you are receiving a
postgraduate student loan
from the Student Loans Company you can set up an instalment plan in line with your loan payments. This instalment plan will be available once we have received confirmation from the Student Loans Company that your loan has been approved.
The postgraduate loan instalment plan is three instalments by direct debit from a current account. Payments are taken on the first of the month:
one third payable two months after start month,
one third payable five months after start month,
one third payable eight months after start month.
Invoices for sponsors and employers
If your fees are being paid by a third party or organisation (for example employer) and they require an invoice, payment needs to be made upfront for each year of study and you will need to follow the
fees process for sponsored students
.
Other online courses
If your online course does not allow module by module payments, you cannot make payments through the online store and must follow the
standard University of Leeds payment procedures
.

Types of postgraduate course | University of Leeds
We offer several different types of taught postgraduate courses.
Master of Arts (MA) is usually awarded in subjects categorised as the arts or social sciences, such as history or education.
Master of Science (MSc) is usually awarded in subjects categorised as the sciences, such as biology or engineering.
Master of Research (MRes) is an advanced, research-based degree, which helps prepare you for progression to a PhD or a career where research skills are required.
Postgraduate Diploma (PGDip) and a Postgraduate Certificate (PGCert) offer Masters-level knowledge without a dissertation. A PGDip is more extensive than a PGCert.
Not all types are available in every subject – please check our
Course Search
for details.

Living costs and budgeting | University of Leeds
To make sure you have enough money for your accommodation, living and study costs at university, it’s a good idea to plan your budget early.
The information on this page is provided as a guideline only
, based on average spending. You should
calculate your own budget
.
If you are an international student, and you have met
financial requirements for your visa
, you should still work out a personal budget separately.
Budget for the amount you would need without getting a job. You may be able to work during your studies, but it will depend on the demands of your course and, if you are an international student,
whether your visa allows you to work in the UK
.
Be aware that living costs may change and be affected by changes in currency exchange rates.
Estimated costs per week
The following tables are estimates for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available. The actual amount will depend on your accommodation type and availability, and your lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
All University accommodation costs include household bills and (except family accommodation) gym membership. Some private accommodation costs include household bills.

Estimated cost per week
University accommodation, self-catered

University accommodation, catered
£205 to £273

£110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications)

Estimated cost per week
Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products
£31 to £38

£14 to £17

Calculate your own budget
Visit the Save the Student website to find budget calculators and advice.
You can use the following list to start researching costs you might need to budget for:
Tuition fees.
University accommodation
or
private accommodation
. If you plan to bring your family, read
information on family accommodation and the costs
.
Furniture and household items, for example for cooking, if you choose private accommodation that doesn’t include them.
Household bills, including energy (gas and/or electricity), water and internet, if not included in your accommodation. These are included in most University accommodation and sometimes included in private accommodation, but not always, so you should check.
Groceries such as food and cleaning supplies.
Buying a laptop (unless you are bringing a reliable laptop suitable for university use with you).
Guidance about bringing your laptop to university

and
your flight to the UK and travel to Leeds
, if you’re an international student.
Travel to visit home or family during breaks (which may include international travel) and
local transport around Leeds
.
Childcare costs
, if you plan to bring your family.
General study costs, such as printing, photocopying and stationery. You can borrow books from our libraries and use University PCs for free.
Costs associated with your course. Some will be optional and depend on your modules, but may include: studying abroad, placements and field trips, conferences and skills days, professional body membership fees, specialist clothing, equipment and project materials. You can check
Course Search
for details.
Mobile phone
.
Activities on campus and in the city. There are also free activities organised by the University and
Leeds University Union

A TV licence

council tax

A global university | University of Leeds
Join our global community, meet interesting people from across the world and develop your global outlook.
Our international approach will also feed into your studies, through internationally focused research and projects or teaching led by academics from all over the world. If you are an undergraduate student you could choose globally-focused

Government postgraduate loans | University of Leeds
If you are ordinarily resident in England or the Republic of Ireland and planning to start your first full-time, part-time or distance learning taught or research Masters course you may be eligible to apply for a
UK government Postgraduate Masters Loan
to help towards your study-related costs.
The loan will be paid directly to you in three instalments in each year of study, and you can choose to use it towards payment of your tuition fee or to help with living costs.
To check your personal and course eligibility, see how much loan you will receive and find out how to apply for the UK government Postgraduate Masters Loan, visit the government’s
Funding for Postgraduate Study
page.
It is important to note that the loans are not available for Integrated Masters courses.
It must be a full, stand-alone postgraduate Masters course. It cannot be a ‘top up’ from a lower level course or a partial postgraduate Masters course undertaken where previous study and/or work experience (Accreditation of Prior Learning) has been taken into account.
If you are funded by the
Student Awards Agency for Scotland (SAAS)
,
Student Finance Wales
or
Student Finance Northern Ireland
, the value, personal and course-related eligibility criteria and method of payment vary. Scottish and Northern Irish applicants may also be eligible for funding for non-Masters programmes.
Registering with the University
After you apply for postgraduate funding and it is approved, the Student Loans Company will notify the University that your funding is in place.
It can take a couple of days to update our student system with this information, so please wait two days before completing step 6 of online registration. This means that you should be able to register without paying your tuition fee at the point of registration.
You will instead be required to set up an instalment plan to pay your tuition fee over three instalments, to coincide with the payment of your Postgraduate Masters loan.
If you have any problems with registering because your postgraduate funding isn’t in place you should
email the Student Funding team via funding@leeds.ac.uk
.
To receive your funding
Students from England, Scotland and Wales will need to have registered and had an
identity check
before the University is able to confirm your registration to the Student Loans Company. Once we confirm your registration you should receive the first instalment of your postgraduate funding within three working days
If you are studying by distance learning you will need to follow the
procedure to get a student card remotely
The funding for students from Northern Ireland is paid as a tuition fee loan, so it will be paid directly to the University of Leeds
Applying for funding
If you are having difficulty applying for your funding, please
email the Student Funding team via funding@leeds.ac.uk
.
Courses with the
Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS)
designation are only added upon request. If you are funded by SAAS you will likely need to contact the Student Funding team to request your course be added to the Student Loans Company system.
When applying for funding, please check the courses available in the drop-down list before contacting the Student Funding Team.
Sharia law and postgraduate loans
Islamic Sharia law prohibits 'Riba' – the paying and receiving of interest for profit. Sometimes the inflation-only interest that is paid on study loans for is seen as Riba (although not all Islamic scholars share this view). Explore more
information about Sharia Law and study loans
.
Other sources of funding
You can also search our
fund your Masters
pages.
Consumer advice site
Money Saving Expert
has guidance on postgraduate student loans.
